chips.title: Margin normalization and wrapped-line joining core
chips.summary: Conflict-based margin classifier, two-or-four-space base detection, and evidence-gated rejoining of terminal-wrapped lines, covered by the Core unit suite.

evidence.message: Initial tray utility scaffold and the introductory-slice specification landed on the first day of the repository.
The two-ratio margin gate was replaced with a conflict-based classifier; a column-zero first line is treated as a selection artifact.
Wrapped-line joining with the wrap signature and an unconditional join hotkey shipped as JOIN-001 through JOIN-005.
Joining now requires word-boundary evidence at the seams (JOIN-001a, JOIN-004a); the Core suite passes on main.

chips.title: Tray app, clipboard privacy policy, and resilience hardening
chips.summary: Tray-only WinForms app with owner-first source attribution, preserved clipboard privacy formats, plain-text-only rewrites, and five adversarial defects fixed and recorded.

evidence.message: Tray application, clipboard listener, single-instance guard, and configuration store were part of the initial scaffold.
Resilience run reproduced four defects (large items, hidden retries, stale overwrite, lost rich formats); all four were fixed in the installed build.
Clipboard history flyout freeze fixed by debouncing clipboard work off the notification path; the resilience report records the root cause.

chips.title: v0.1.0 release with installer, hosted CI, and closed installer runbook
chips.summary: Per-user installer with a Start-with-Windows toggle, hosted Windows CI, a tag-built release workflow, and the published 0.1.0 artifact with all fifteen runbook steps recorded.

evidence.message: Startup registration and the Start-with-Windows tray toggle landed alongside the first installer work.
Hosted Windows build-and-test workflow merged; local, pull-request, and main runs all passed the same 113 tests.
v0.1.0 tagged and built by the release workflow from the tagged commit, with a checksum published beside the unsigned installer.
Installer runbook steps 1-15 recorded on main, including reinstall-while-running against the published artifact; the box is back on the released build.

chips.title: v0.1 evidence-backed Windows proof
chips.summary: The proof plan for v0.1: automated baseline and installer proof are recorded; the manual functional clipboard matrix is the open remainder before a proof report can be written.

evidence.message: Proof plan defined against the implementation baseline: automated acceptance criteria, POC questions, and nineteen manual matrix steps.
Functional proof ledger moved into tracked docs so its unrun state is visible in a clone; installer proof and automated baseline are the recorded parts.
Repository review: no commits since the runbook closeout on 2026-08-29 and the working tree holds only an ignore-file edit; the manual matrix is still unrun.

chips.title: Run the v0.1 functional proof ledger
chips.summary: Nineteen manual clipboard cases (M01-M19) have never been run against a 0.1.0 build; they need an operator at a Windows keyboard across terminals, editors, and history.

evidence.message: Seeded from the v0.1 proof ledger during the 2026-09-01 chip-board refresh.
Still unrun. The BASELINE row is stale (37 tests then, 119 on main now) and must be re-run first; registry-backed cases need an interactive shell, not an agent session.

chips.title: Proof report, spec sync, and the next release
chips.summary: Summarize the proof run into a report, record the POC-08 rich-format decision, sync the spec and README support boundary, and tag the next release through the release checklist.

evidence.message: Derived from the completion criteria of the proof plan and the release checklist; the unreleased section of the changelog is empty.

chips.title: Source fingerprint matrix and focused-control detection
chips.summary: Build a source-fingerprint matrix across real terminals and agent hosts, then add focused-control detection to tell editor-integrated terminals apart from editor copies.

evidence.message: Listed under planned next steps in the README together with moving clipboard work to a dedicated STA thread and tray last-action status.

chips.title: Rich-format normalization, signed packaging, and image export
chips.summary: Evaluate consistent HTML and RTF normalization, signed or MSI packaging, remote-desktop clipboard behavior, and the unmerged clipboard-image export experiment for WSL.

evidence.message: Rich-format and packaging items come from the README limitations; the image-export branch has two commits from 2026-08-21 that never reached main.
